newsitem.title: USA: Cohen says sex harassment problems can be solved.
newsitem.headline: Cohen says sex harassment problems can be solved.

text.p: Defence Secretary William Cohen said Friday he was "confident" sex harassment and recruiting problems plaguing the military could be solved.

After a tour of Fort Jackson, the Army's largest recruit training centre, the former U.S. senator listed his priorities as people, readiness and modernisation and said "good training is the key to all three."
Cohen, who took over his new job Jan. 24, played down recent reports that the number of high school graduates entering the military had declined.

"With the Army being aware that there's been a slight decrease in the numbers of high school graduates coming into the service, they will make recommendations in terms of ways we can try to increase opportunities," he said.

Cohen also said he believed the Army had faced the issue of sex abuse and harassment scandals that have rocked the military. The military has faced an ongoing sex harassment probe that began with allegations from women at a training centre in Aberdeen, Maryland. Drill instructors have been charged with rape or harassment of female recruits.

They are trying to get out in front of the issue. They are dealing with it, I think, in a very proactive fashion," Cohen said. He reiterated that he had not seen any evidence that the military's policy of generally training men and women together should be reversed.

"(From) what I have witnessed today it seems to be working quite well," he said. "My position is that I'm open to any suggestions but I have to be persuaded there's compelling evidence as to why integrated training should not be continued."

He said the Army needed to find out the extent of sexual harassment within the system. "We don't know the answer to how serious the problem is. If it's a problem ... we want to know how deeply that problem goes," he said.
"If we find that it is deeply ingrained then we will have to take a lot very of aggressive measures to correct it. I'm satisfied that the Army has responded in the appropriate fashion."
The tour of Fort Jackson, coupled with a tour on Thursday of Lackland Air Base in Texas, marked Cohen's first visits to military facilities since he took the new post.
